headline: Tk 6.67cr corruption: Court frames charges against ex-NBR official Matiur
summary: The former official is accused of amassing illegal wealth of Tk 5.4 crore and concealing assets worth Tk 1.27 crore.
details: A Dhaka court has framed charges against former National Board of Revenue (NBR) member Matiur Rahman in a corruption case involving illegal wealth and concealed assets.
Matiur, who is currently in jail, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out by Judge BM Tarikul Kabir of the Divisional Special Judge's Court.
The charges stem from allegations that he amassed illegal wealth of Tk 5.4 crore and concealed information on assets worth Tk 1.27 crore.
The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on December 15, 2024, and submitted the charge sheet on February 3, 2025.
Matiur was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police on January 15, 2025, from the Bashundhara Residential Area.
He previously served as the president of the NBR's Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal.
He gained public notoriety in June 2024 after a video of his son purchasing a goat for Tk 15 lakh for Eid went viral on social media.
The 'goat controversy' led to widespread reports on the family's luxury cars, expensive watches, and property holdings.
The court has set September 14 for the recording of testimony from prosecution witnesses.
According to ACC lawyers, two additional corruption cases involving Matiur are currently under investigation.
caption:
From a Tk 15 lakh goat to a Tk 6.67 crore corruption case. A former NBR official now faces trial.

A Dhaka court has framed charges against former National Board of Revenue (NBR) member Matiur Rahman in a corruption case involving illegal wealth and concealed assets.

Matiur, who is currently in jail, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out by Judge BM Tarikul Kabir of the Divisional Special Judge's Court.

The charges stem from allegations that he amassed illegal wealth of Tk 5.4 crore and concealed information on assets worth Tk 1.27 crore.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed the case on December 15, 2024, and submitted the charge sheet on February 3, 2025.

Matiur was arrested by the Detective Branch (DB) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police on January 15, 2025, from the Bashundhara Residential Area.

He previously served as the president of the NBR's Customs, Excise and VAT Appellate Tribunal.

He gained public notoriety in June 2024 after a video of his son purchasing a goat for Tk 15 lakh for Eid went viral on social media.

The 'goat controversy' led to widespread reports on the family's luxury cars, expensive watches, and property holdings.

The court has set September 14 for the recording of testimony from prosecution witnesses.

According to ACC lawyers, two additional corruption cases involving Matiur are currently under investigation.

headline: 847 dead as measles outbreak kills three in 24 hours
summary: Nearly nine in 10 affected families are pushed into debt due to the ongoing health crisis.
details: A severe measles outbreak has claimed the lives of 847 people, with three deaths reported in the last 24 hours alone.
The crisis is taking a heavy toll on families, with nearly 90% of affected households being pushed into debt to afford care.
The rapid spread of the virus is causing significant strain on healthcare resources and family finances.
Health officials are monitoring the situation as the death toll continues to rise.
